signature: test(http2): expose lost peer completion and error causes
root_command: scripts/dev/with-cargo-lock.sh cargo nextest run -p phantom-net --all-targets --all-features --locked --no-fail-fast -E 'test(http2::tests::request_body_cancellation::) | test(http2::tests::driver_lifecycle::)'
phase: baseline only; source frozen awaiting actual native red and independent review
limits: No Cargo/build/runtime execution, production source edits, push, rebase or merge. All predicted counts require actual Windows/Linux execution.

Control task completion uses pinned AbortHandle.is_finished guarantee for destructor completion; this is not an observed original joined outcome after its handle was lost. Abort guards bound cleanup and request abort on unexpected test exits; explicit bounded completion precedes expected negative assertions.
100ms quiet observations are finite, after actual exchanges with client/body/runtime retained. No permanent OS/resource leak claim.

CompletedPeerFault is an intentionally injected typed sentinel after real protocol readiness, not an actual wire INTERNAL_ERROR/remote failure. Only the upload reset control sends actual RST_STREAM and requires remote/reset classification.

Error::source is linear: simultaneous-cause canaries independently check primary RecvError and exact tagged peer diagnostic. Typed peer H2 source has a separate positive; final cleanup-type retention additionally requires independent source inspection of concrete aggregation.
Local-runtime shutdown in original plain-thread control remains a different enclosing ownership boundary; no permanent survival claim.
Source identities are exact raw Git bytes. Indentation projections prove named mechanical extractions only; supporting API reads remain partial, not vendor-wide review.

Original reset peer and literal upload/tail oracles are preserved; first lifecycle caller now captures primary result before equivalent early-return helper, not a completed-peer remedy. Remaining local/Tokio callers remain unfixed until native baseline.
